# #827 — tier-lane: no test asserts the tier_lane_denied warn line

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: bug
Created: 2026-08-26T19:42:47Z
Updated: 2026-08-26T19:42:47Z

---

Filed 2026-08-26 by the #780 drain lane (native Claude head session, `780-sweep-session2`), draining the session-3 handoff (PR #824) per `_ob/skills/handoff-author/_DOCS/steps/01-drain.md`. Sourced from the critical self-review of PR #819 (merged), which named the gap and deferred it because that lane held existing tests unmodified.

## The gap

Nothing in the suite asserts that `server/tools/tier-lane.ts` emits its `tier_lane_denied` warn line on a namespace denial.

## Why it matters — the concrete failure it would hide

PR #819 refactored `tier-lane.ts` to the lint standard and, in doing so, faced a reuse decision: take the shared `authorize` helper from `memory-helpers.ts`, or keep a local `authorizeTierLane`. The shapes are close but not identical field for field — **the shared `authorize` emits no denial log.** Calling it would have silently dropped the `tier_lane_denied` warn line.

From #819's own self-review:

> Missing/weak tests: no test asserts the `tier_lane_denied` warn line is emitted, which is the one behavior most at risk from the reuse decision above. That gap is what made me keep the local helper rather than take the shared `authorize` — the suite would not have caught the dropped log.

So the swap was avoided by a human reading the two helpers side by side, not by a check. The suite passed either way. That is the defect: an observability behavior with no pin, sitting directly under a refactor pattern the #780 sweep applies file after file, where "replace the local helper with the shared one" is exactly the kind of tidy-looking change a future lane is likely to make.

This is not unique to `tier-lane.ts`. #819 records that every tool in this family that logs a denial keeps a local helper for the same reason — `promotion.ts`, `adjacent-context.ts`, `citation-recall.ts`, `promote-entry.ts`. All of them are one shared-helper swap away from silently losing their denial log, and it is plausible none of them are pinned either.

## Ask

Add a pinning test that drives `tier_lane` to a namespace denial and asserts the `tier_lane_denied` warn line is emitted — event name and the fields that make it useful, not merely "a warn happened".

Prove it red first: with the test in place, swapping `authorizeTierLane` for the shared `authorize` must fail it. A test that passes under both helpers has not pinned anything, and given the whole point of this issue is that the current suite passes under both, red-first is the acceptance criterion rather than a nicety.

## Worth checking while in there

Whether the sibling denial-logging tools listed above have the same hole. If they do, say so in a comment here rather than silently widening this lane — sizing that is a separate call.

## Constraints

- Test evidence is `bun run test:isolated`, never bare `bun test` (rule 10, `_DOCS/HANDOFF-RULES.md`): Postgres tests skip silently without `OPENBRAIN_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, and full-suite runs against the dogfood database return a different failure count each time (#614).
- The pre-commit gate lints staged files whole (rule 25), so touching a test file with pre-existing findings means clearing them in the same lane.
